target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, standard STS dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: You lead with 20.5% and call 9% the floor; I would put those the other way round. The 20.5% is a 44-patient subset of a 1988-2011 registry scored by local investigators, and the p=0.04 attached to it compares dedifferentiated against conventional histology rather than testing whether chemotherapy helped anybody. Your case against MAP-type intensification lands, but both supports are localized-disease datasets (the SEER cohort excluded distant disease at diagnosis, the pooled OR 1.25 is 556 localized patients), so neither settles a metastatic first-line question in either direction.

target_intervention_label: IDH1/IDH2 hotspot testing on a comprehensive DNA/RNA panel
comment: You caught the thing most people miss, that the 23.1% belongs to 13 conventional-histology patients. What is missing is the other 8: they were dosed in the same phase 1, they were non-conventional, and their responses appear in neither the 2020 report nor the 2025 follow-up. That is a selective-outcome-reporting domain rather than a hole in the literature, and it changes what a positive IDH1 call means for her, since the drug has been given in her subtype and the result simply was not published.

target_intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture (not oncologic resection)
comment: The split between fixation and oncologic resection is right and I made the same one. One point of symmetry: no survival association for resection in high-grade dedifferentiated disease is itself a subgroup interaction analysis inside a 200-patient SEER cohort, so it withdraws the benefit claim without proving futility, and it deserves the same suspicion you aim at the Japanese registry's 51.0% versus 19.3%. Neither paper measured the operation you are recommending, and not one cohort in this dossier reports surgical morbidity for pelvic fixation in metastatic disease.

target_intervention_label: Pembrolizumab, biomarker-conditional, second line
comment: A decade of post-marketing data describes toxicity, not benefit, and here the safety record is quietly doing the ranking work. The efficacy base is 1 of 5 in SARC028, inside a bone cohort whose primary endpoint failed at 2 of 40 and whose responder the primary report never subtypes, plus 1 PR of 5 in the Bui series. Keep the pick on the grounds you actually give, that a TMB-high or MSI-high call makes it on-label, but the number travelling with it should be stated as five patients rather than as a 20% response rate.

target_intervention_label: TAPUR: marketed targeted agents by genomic match (NCT02693535)
comment: TAPUR buys protocol structure and familiar toxicity management, which is what you claim for it, and that is the whole of what it buys. The design is a basket of single-arm matched cohorts and no chondrosarcoma cohort result exists, so this is an access decision carrying no efficacy estimate at all. At rank 5 that is defensible, provided nobody downstream reads the NCT number as though it were data.

target_intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, pushed to osteosarcoma-type intensity if measured fitness allows
comment: The 29% is 23 patients. It is the metastatic subgroup of EURO-B.O.S.S., p=0.12 against the 46% localized figure, in an uncontrolled protocol that enrolled only patients judged fit for intensive chemotherapy, which is precisely the selection that manufactures a five-year tail. The internal structure argues against you as well: 63% of that cohort reached surgical complete remission, and the significant split in the paper is the remission one (49% versus 23%, p=0.004), so the tail may be tracking resectability rather than the regimen.

target_intervention_label: IACS-6274 (glutaminase-1 inhibitor), phase 1 NCT05039801
comment: Rank 2 for a mechanism with no clinical result in any chondrosarcoma patient anywhere. The support is a single cell-line paper reporting that glutaminase expression rises with grade (p=0.001) and that sensitivity did not sort by IDH status, with no in-vivo chondrosarcoma arm; the second half is a null finding you are using as an eligibility argument, which is fair, but nobody should mistake it for evidence of effect. Escalation also means she could be assigned a dose level that nobody involved expects to work.

target_intervention_label: Sunitinib plus nivolumab, off-label at first progression
comment: One PR among 4 dedifferentiated patients, in a 40-patient cohort with a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis, 17% discontinuation for toxicity and ORR 5% overall. You list both halves and rank it third regardless, in a woman whose ECOG 2 has never been measured by anyone. The microenvironment work in this same dossier points away from the axis: macrophages were the dominant population, a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was independently prognostic at p<0.01, and depleting T cells accelerated growth in the immunocompetent rat model.

target_intervention_label: Abemaciclib on NCT04040205, pre-positioned now for the post-anthracycline line
comment: Same pick as mine, different load-bearing wall. The palbociclib intraosseous result you lean on never reported CDKN2A status of its lines and carries a 2023 figure correction (pmid 36803557), so it cannot support the biomarker inference; what makes NCT04040205 worth a seat is the registered primary endpoint, central Rb immunohistochemistry rather than a local read, and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named as its own eligible histology. No CDK4/6 inhibitor has a published chondrosarcoma efficacy result, which is worth saying in the row rather than only in the concerns.

target_intervention_label: CD276 (B7-H3) CAR-T on NCT04433221, conditional on a high B7-H3 H-score
comment: The 96% is prevalence off a 24-specimen dedifferentiated tissue microarray with a Merck-employed author, and prevalence is the wrong quantity for this class: Majzner's activity was greatly diminished against low-expressing targets and the avidity work puts a measurable density threshold on it. The only H-score measurement in existence places chondrosarcoma lowest of any sarcoma subtype, median 60 against 175 for osteosarcoma (n=133), so your stated condition will most likely fail. NCT04433221 also gives the CAR alongside low-dose chemotherapy and an irradiated tumour-cell vaccine, n=20, one site, safety as the primary endpoint, so a response there could not be attributed to the CAR anyway.

target_intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy now; dosing intensity decided with her once fitness is measured
comment: Quoting 9% to 20.5% as a range is more honest than most of this table, but the two ends do not deserve equal weight in a consent conversation. The 20.5% is a 44-patient subset treated 1988-2011 with local response assessment; the 9% comes from five academic centres treating 2004-2022, and it arrives attached to a metastatic median OS of 7.2 months with nobody alive at five years. If she hears one number before she agrees to anything, it should be the modern one, with the older figure offered as the optimistic bound rather than as half of a midpoint.

target_intervention_label: Comprehensive DNA/RNA panel with full IDH1 codon 132 / IDH2 codon 140/172 coverage, ordered on archival tissue now
comment: This is the only IDH row on the board that states out loud that NCT06127407 and NCT04278781 exclude her histology by name, whatever the assay returns. One reinforcement for the conversation you are planning: the 8 non-conventional patients dosed in the ivosidenib phase 1 have no published response data in either the 2020 paper or the 2025 follow-up, so the silence about her subtype is an unreported outcome, not an untried drug. The rest of the row survives contact with its sources, which I cannot say for much here.

target_intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture at a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre, timed against trial washouts
comment: The idea that fixing the acetabulum could raise her measured ECOG and reopen the trial doors the assumption is closing is the most useful thing anyone put on this table, and it has no supporting row. Nothing in the dossier measures performance status before and after periacetabular stabilisation, and no cohort here counts surgical morbidity at all, so as written it is a mechanism argument of the kind I would refuse from risktaker. Separately, centre volume tracking with outcome in pelvic bone sarcoma is not measured in anything you cite; pmid 30559960 is 31 patients from one UK centre with no volume comparison in it.

target_intervention_label: IACS-6274 phase 1 (NCT05039801): make the MD Anderson call this week, enroll only if she chooses it knowing the numbers
comment: Ranking the phone call rather than the drug is the defensible version of this, and it is what separates you from risktaker putting the same protocol at rank 2. The evidence underneath is still one in-vitro paper with no chondrosarcoma in-vivo arm and no clinical result for the class in this disease, and the ECOG 0-1 bar with no deterioration over the preceding fortnight means screening only becomes a real question after somebody examines her. The deliverable here is the screening answer, and the row should read that way downstream.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, with or without ifosfamide or cisplatin
comment: Refusing to assert a category you could not read is the right call and I want it on the record as such. Two problems with the figures: the EURO-B.O.S.S. median OS of 24 months (95% CI 22-25) belongs to the whole 57-patient cohort, localized patients included, 63% of whom reached surgical complete remission, so it is not a metastatic first-line number; and a confidence interval that tight around a median in 57 patients should draw a second look on its own. Your population-swap observation about the SEER and pooled-review rows is the sharpest thing said about the chemotherapy fork by anybody.

target_intervention_label: Referral to a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre
comment: Rank 2 with nothing readable behind it, and you say so, which is more than the citation list does: pmid 17720491 is a prognosis cohort and pmid 30559960 is a 31-patient single-centre series, and neither measures referral or centre volume against anything. The case-level argument does carry the action, since expert bone pathology, periacetabular surgeons and trial screening sit inside the same institutions and the accessibility row says self-referral needs no letter. What it does not carry is the position, because a reader will register rank 2 well before they reach your disclaimer.

target_intervention_label: Periacetabular resection and reconstruction, or orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture
comment: Your rationale cites SEER HR 0.481 as a dataset supporting resection; that is the all-comers estimate from the same paper whose interaction test found no association in dedifferentiated, high-grade disease. Be symmetric about it though, because the subgroup that removes the benefit claim is still a subgroup and it establishes nothing about futility. The larger issue is the label: resection and stabilisation are different operations, one of them reached its margins by hindquarter amputation in the closest pelvic series, and putting both on one rank lets the wrong one inherit the other's justification.

target_intervention_label: IDH1/IDH2 sequencing within comprehensive DNA/RNA profiling of the dedifferentiated component
comment: Workup and trial key rather than therapy is the correct frame, and quoting olutasidenib at a median PFS of 1.5 months instead of ivosidenib's 23.1% is the difference between citing her subtype and citing somebody else's. One thing that strengthens your refusal to support off-label ivosidenib: the 8 non-conventional patients dosed in NCT02073994 have never had their responses reported, so the objection rests on selective outcome reporting and not only on a thin biological argument. Requiring that the dedifferentiated component is the tissue sequenced is the operational detail the rest of us left out.

target_intervention_label: Palliative radiotherapy and local measures at the fracture site, with early specialist palliative care alongside
comment: An odd result worth stating plainly: the ASCO palliative-care recommendation sitting at your rank 5 is the best-evidenced item anyone put on this board, and it ranks below four things built on retrospective cohorts. The rest of the row is thinner than its neighbour, since cementoplasty and percutaneous fixation have no evidence row in this dossier at all and the non-union caution comes from a rat model. You read the abstract rather than the recommendation table and said so; I have worked mostly from abstracts too, including the EURO-B.O.S.S. per-term toxicity table, which is paywalled and which I have not seen.

target_intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, pushed to osteosarcoma-type intensity if measured fitness allows
comment: The risktaker's round-2 correction of my ordering lands and I take it: the panel rides archival tissue while the operative date has to thread 4-week washouts, so fixation is the rate-limiting booking, the board should hear that as a sequence change rather than a rank swap, and the operative specimen gets banked for molecular pathology while she is already under anaesthesia. What I will not take is 'the most intensive regimen she clears': the 0.8 efficacy weight and the empty veto list are inferred defaults per preferences.json, so an entry gate she passes is not a bill she has agreed to, and both regimens go in front of her with their numbers (pmid:33990016, pmid:34648466) once the ECOG and LVEF are measured. Ranks 2 through 5 carrying zero chondrosarcoma clinical results is one reading of 'pursue all possible therapeutic options'; the concensusite's no-bets slate is the opposite reading, and nobody has asked her which one she meant.

target_intervention_label: Pembrolizumab, biomarker-conditional, second line
comment: Targeting rank 4 rather than the chemo consensus because this is where the assumed ECOG hardens into a fact: 'a different risk conversation for an assumed-ECOG-2 patient' lets an intake assumption pre-decide monotherapy over the combination, when the conservative's own rank 1 rightly says nothing starts until the ECOG is measured. The grade 5 pneumonitis and 17% toxicity discontinuation (pmid:39540661) are real, and she may hear them and refuse, but that refusal belongs to her against a measured number, and the number may move if fixation does its job. Pembrolizumab held in reserve, biomarker-conditional, I co-sign; my qualification is that a patient who asked for everything gets shown the harder option with its price, not spared it by an assumption doing a measurement's work.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy at standard soft-tissue-sarcoma dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: 'Plan against the 9%' works for stop rules and restaging calendars and fails as the number she hears: the bracket's ends differ by treatment era, response assessment and an n=44 subset (pmid:24099780 versus pmid:37174084), so what she should be told is 9 to 20.5 with why the ends disagree, and choosing either end on her behalf is a decision she has not been in the room for. That conversation has not happened, and it sits on top of a longer unsaid list: the 5-to-7-month metastatic medians, both IDH trials excluding her subtype by name (nct:NCT06127407, nct:NCT04278781), both particle trials closed to her because of the lung nodules. The one mercy in this row is that doxorubicin needs no trial seat and no prior-authorisation fight, so the telling can happen this week.

target_intervention_label: Palliative radiotherapy and local measures at the fracture site, with early specialist palliative care alongside
comment: Not a vote against early palliative care, which the row defends well, and I will defend the rank-2 referral against the risktaker's dissent: that single address opens expert pathology, the periacetabular surgeons and the trial screens at once, and may open more doors than any drug on anyone's list. The dissent is arithmetic: zero of five seats hold an experimental therapy against prefers_trials set true and her one recorded sentence, when TAPUR's ECOG 0-2 bar (nct:NCT02693535) is among the very few she may clear as written and the treatment-naive chondrosarcoma-named phase 1 (nct:NCT05039801) at minimum deserved the phone call. This no-bets slate and the risktaker's four-seats-with-no-chondrosarcoma-results slate both claim 'pursue all possible therapeutic options'; only one can be what she meant, and asking her costs a conversation, not a seat.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, standard STS dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: Standard STS dosing is where I land too, and the deliverability read makes it stronger: 18 of 57 in EURO-B.O.S.S.'s own fitness-selected cohort never reached 6 of the 9 planned cycles (pmid:33990016), which is a fact about the regimen rather than about frail patients. Nothing I could reach attaches an intensity to anthracycline in this histology, I verified no category in round 1 and still assert none, and both comparative attempts are null (pmid:34648466, pmid:38275833). On what is actually readable, this row is the closest thing on the board to what practice is.

target_intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture (not oncologic resection)
comment: Their qualification of my rank 3 was fair and I take it: I let stabilisation and resection share one label, and the resection survival signal sits in conventional and grade II disease with nothing in dedifferentiated or grade III (pmid:30762691), while the nearest pelvic series bought its margins with hindquarter amputation (pmid:30559960). Fixation alone is the operation I should have named, and this row names it. The sequencing rule inside it, fixation before any radiotherapy to that bone (pmid:23606416), is the one recommendation here with a mechanism behind it and nothing readable in any guideline against it; the PI should carry it as a standing constraint, not a preference.

target_intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, pushed to osteosarcoma-type intensity if measured fitness allows
comment: We agree on the drug at rank 1; 'the most intensive regimen she clears' is the clause I decline to call endorsed, same as round 1, and I could verify no document that underwrites it. The comparative attempts are null (pmid:34648466, pmid:38275833) and deliverability now cuts the same way, since 18 of 57 in the fitness-selected EURO-B.O.S.S. cohort never completed 6 of 9 cycles (pmid:33990016), so intensity was already failing in the population selected to receive it. Where the record is silent my position is to say so, and on intensification it is silent everywhere I could read.

target_intervention_label: IACS-6274 (glutaminase-1 inhibitor), phase 1 NCT05039801
comment: Two concessions first: a pending IDH result does not gate this, since cell-line sensitivity did not sort by genotype and expression tracked grade (pmid:29576625), and NCT05039801 as the one treatment-naive protocol naming chondrosarcoma deserved a line on my slate; the advocate's rank 4, the call rather than the drug, is the row I should have written. What I do not concede is the shape of the slate, because trial enrollment is the consensus route to experimental therapy and every reachable seat in this screen is screened and delivered through the same bone-sarcoma centres, so my rank 2 referral is the enrollment mechanism, not a seat spent on a non-treatment. Rank 2 for escalation-phase monotherapy with no clinical result in this disease is still first-line time spent on a dose-finding question, and that part stays contested.

target_intervention_label: Sunitinib plus nivolumab, off-label at first progression
comment: Targeting rank 3 because it is the clearest off-label move on the board: an unendorsed combination whose cohort logged a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis and 17% toxicity discontinuation against a dedifferentiated signal of 1 PR in 4 (pmid:39540661). Marketed means buyable, not endorsed, and the payer fight the risktaker predicts is the system pricing that exact gap. If a checkpoint route stays on the table at all, the conservative's biomarker-conditional monotherapy is the version a label could ever stand behind.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy at standard soft-tissue-sarcoma dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: On the 9 versus 20.5 dispute, both sides are right about different things: the ends of the bracket differ by era and response assessment, as the risktaker says, and the modern figure is still the honest planning number, as this row says (pmid:37174084, pmid:24099780). Guideline silence settles less than either side wants; anthracycline is given first-line in this histology whichever figure you believe, so the bracket governs the consent conversation and the restaging calendar rather than the treatment choice. It decides nothing about intensity, and neither does any document I could reach.

target_intervention_label: IACS-6274 phase 1 (NCT05039801): make the MD Anderson call this week, enroll only if she chooses it knowing the numbers
comment: I aim at rank 4 rather than the chemo consensus because my concession lives here: the call rather than the drug is the version of NCT05039801 that belonged on my slate, and the advocate wrote the row I failed to write. It survives the sceptics because the deliverable is a screening answer, the cost is a phone call, and first-line anthracycline does not wait. One addition from my side of the table: the centre that screens her for this protocol is the referral I ranked second, so the two rows are one act.

target_intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture at a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre, timed against trial washouts
comment: Rank 3 as my target because the centre routing inside it is my rank 2 under another name, and the unsourced objection to both was fair, so I went and sourced it: in the nationwide French NETSARC cohorts, pre-treatment review by a specialist sarcoma board and surgery at a reference centre were each associated with better survival (pmid:29117335, pmid:31081028; verified by title, journal and year this run, and neither is bone-sarcoma-specific, which I will not pretend away). Add the case-level fact that expert pathology, the periacetabular surgeons, the trial screens and the particle-therapy second opinion all sit at the same address, and I keep both the substance and the rank, conceding only the critic's point that a reader meets the rank before the disclaimer. The washout arithmetic here is right too; the operative date and the trial calendar belong in the same hands.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, standard STS dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: Same drug, and I concede most of the intensity fight: the 29% I leaned on is a 23-patient fitness-selected subgroup at p=0.12 and cannot carry the bet I placed on it (pmid:33990016). But 'no survival edge to pay for' rests on SEER (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.49-1.12; pmid:34648466) and the pooled OR 1.25 (pmid:38275833), both perioperative localized datasets that never asked the first-line metastatic question. Unproven is not disproven; once the ECOG and LVEF are measured numbers, doxorubicin plus ifosfamide still belongs in front of a patient who asked for everything.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy at standard soft-tissue-sarcoma dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: Her EURO-B.O.S.S. autopsy lands and I take the hit: p=0.12 in 23 fitness-selected metastatic patients was never a foundation, and I built on it anyway (pmid:33990016). 'Plan against the 9%' is the part I won't sign: that floor comes from a five-centre series whose own first-line regimens were osteosarcoma-protocol-style (pmid:37174084), so the 9-to-20.5 bracket separates eras and response assessment, not doses, and choosing the floor is as much a decision as my choosing the ceiling was. A bracket that wide argues for stacking options behind chemotherapy, which is where the rest of my list lives.

target_intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture at a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre, timed against trial washouts
comment: Her rank 3, not her rank 1, because this is the row that corrects me: I left the fracture unranked, and she is right that fixation is the one move that could turn the assumed ECOG 2 into a measured 0-1, which is exactly what opens the escalation seat I put second (nct:NCT05039801). My quarrel is the order: the panel at her rank 2 rides archival tissue and waits for nobody, while the operative date has to thread 4-week protocol washouts, so fixation is the rate-limiting step and belongs above the testing. In a disease with a 5-month metastatic median (pmid:17720491), the slowest-to-schedule move goes first.

target_intervention_label: Referral to a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre
comment: The referral itself is sound, and it is the screen door to every protocol I want her near, but a rank-2 slot is a treatment seat, and between this row and rank 5 the list spends two of five seats on things that treat nothing, leaving zero experimental therapy for a patient whose one recorded preference is to pursue all possible therapeutic options. The single protocol that writes chondrosarcoma in as its own treatment-naive population went unranked (nct:NCT05039801), and it does not even wait on the pending IDH result, because glutaminase expression tracks grade rather than genotype (pmid:29576625). Sequencing prudence is fine; a slate with no bet in it is not what she asked this board for.

target_intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, pushed to osteosarcoma-type intensity if measured fitness allows
comment: 'The most intensive regimen she clears' prices the entry gate, not the bill: even EURO-B.O.S.S.'s chemo-fit cohort had 30% fail to reach 6 of 9 cycles, the 29% metastatic five-year OS rests on roughly 23 patients with no comparator (pmid:33990016), and both comparative estimates are null (SEER HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.49-1.12; pooled OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.80-1.94). Ifosfamide and cisplatin add renal, neurologic and haematologic cost on organ function nobody has measured, in a disease whose median runs 5 to 7 months. The missing baseline runs down the whole slate: ranks 2-5 carry zero chondrosarcoma clinical results, and rank 3 rests on a 1-of-4 subgroup from a cohort that logged a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis with 17% toxicity discontinuation (pmid:39540661), all ranked before an ECOG, an echo or a creatinine exists.

target_intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy at standard soft-tissue-sarcoma dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
comment: Planning against the 9% (pmid:37174084) rather than the 20.5% is right, and it sets the toxicity budget: at that response rate I would give single-agent doxorubicin, restage after two cycles, and agree stop rules before cycle one, since by then a non-responder has spent about a fifth of the 7.2-month median on treatment weeks. The point that neither anchor cohort reports one per-term AE rate is the sharpest line in the file; the entire toxicity ledger here is imported from other sarcomas. The pembrolizumab tracing also cuts against my own rank 4: a pick conditioned on an untested biomarker plus a responder nobody can subtype (pmid:28988646) is thinner than I priced it, and the critic's version of that row is the honest one.

target_intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture at a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre, timed against trial washouts
comment: Rank 3 rather than the chemo consensus, because the fixation-raises-her-ECOG argument carries a lot of load with no morbidity data under it: neither registry series (pmid:40613902, pmid:30762691) reports a single surgical complication, so the downside of periacetabular surgery in metastatic disease is uncounted, not small. Recovery runs in weeks against a 5-to-7-month median, and a badly picked operative date plus the 4-week washouts closes trial doors instead of opening them; the ECOG can as easily be spent as raised. Fixation before any radiotherapy (atrophic non-union, pmid:23606416) I co-sign; my qualification is that the operation's price needs stating to her as plainly as the chemo numbers.

target_intervention_label: Periacetabular resection and reconstruction, or orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture
comment: Targeting rank 3 because the label keeps 'periacetabular resection and reconstruction' on the menu, and that half should come off: the resection survival signal sits in conventional and grade II disease with no association in dedifferentiated or grade III (pmid:30762691), and the closest pelvic series bought its margins with hindquarter amputation (pmid:32564907). Offering internal hemipelvectomy to a metastatic dedifferentiated patient with unmeasured fitness is the same population swap the concensusite's own chemo row warns against. The sequencing points, fixation settled before anything irradiates that bone and the washout calendar kept open, I endorse as written.
